title: Directive-registry digest normalization (CRLF/LF) - retire the control-plane CI red
objective: Make every directive-registry content digest line-ending-independent (sha256 over CRLF-to-LF-normalized bytes) in the shared computation sites (directive_registry.sha256_file for c2 source digests; validate_directive_compliance.py requirements-content c14 + migration-manifest checks), then re-stamp the six stale manifest digest values (D-032 source-004-amendment + requirements, D-033 source-002-amendment + requirements, D-034 requirements, D-038 requirements) to their LF-normalized values via append-only manifest edits + audit_log entries citing D-040:D-040-R003. Source files IMMUTABLE - zero byte changes to any source-*.md or requirements.json. Local validator EXIT 0 stays; the CI control-plane job (LF checkout) goes green - the standing red retires.
business_reason: D-040-R003 (owner 2026-09-12) authorizes this as ordinary gated control-plane work. The red has masked the control-plane job since the digests were recorded over local CRLF bytes while CI checks out LF; every push wastes a required check and the red hides genuine future control-plane regressions.
inputs: project-control/directives/D-040-scoped-unblocks/source-001.md + requirements.json R003 (the authorizing requirement text; constraint: source files IMMUTABLE, append-only mechanisms only)

CI run 34681382456 control-plane job 103520545751 log (the authoritative failure list: exactly 6 digest mismatches with their LF-normalized 'actual' values - D-032 source-004-amendment 3704add2.., D-032 requirements d8158188.., D-033 source-002-amendment d0ae01b4.., D-033 requirements d2876943.., D-034 requirements dfab73c0.., D-038 requirements 0e9de4cc..)
tools/directive_registry.py (sha256_file ~:386 used by the c2 source-digest check ~:525-532; READ the whole digest path before editing)
tools/test_directive_compliance.py (the adversarial test suite the CI control-plane job runs; extend, never weaken)
.gitattributes (pins directives text eol=lf - WHY CI bytes are LF while local disk is CRLF) + the recorded byte-format trap: local directives manifests/requirements are CRLF on disk

project-control/directives/{D-032-astra-loop-activation-and-review-reconciliation,D-033-supervisor-management-layer,D-034-architecture-context-and-review-skill,D-038-build-product-not-self}/manifest.json (the six digest values to re-stamp + audit_log to append; CRLF on disk, indent conventions preserved byte-for-byte outside the intended edits)
outputs: tools/directive_registry.py (normalized digest computation for registry text artifacts)
tools/validate_directive_compliance.py (same normalization at its digest sites)
tools/test_directive_compliance.py (extended: CRLF/LF equivalence red/green + tamper-still-detected adversarial case)

acceptance_scenarios.input: identical registry-artifact content in CRLF and in LF byte form (test fixtures for a source-*.md and a requirements.json)
acceptance_scenarios.expected: the normalized digest function returns the SAME sha256 for both forms, equal to the sha256 of the LF bytes; RED/GREEN proof required - with the normalization removed (or bypassed), the new test FAILS. Lone-CR (classic-Mac) bytes are also normalized or explicitly rejected - documented either way.

acceptance_scenarios.input: the actual project-control/directives tree - locally (CRLF manifests/requirements on disk) and in CI (LF checkout per .gitattributes)
acceptance_scenarios.expected: python tools/validate_directive_compliance.py --check EXIT 0 locally AND the CI control-plane job passes on the pushed head (the standing red retires). CI is the executable authority for the LF side.

acceptance_scenarios.input: the six re-stamped manifest digest values
acceptance_scenarios.expected: each equals sha256(LF-normalized bytes) of its file, and each matches the 'actual' value the failing CI log reported (prefixes 3704add2 / d8158188 / d0ae01b4 / d2876943 / dfab73c0 / 0e9de4cc) - asserted in the producer report with the full 64-hex values.

acceptance_scenarios.input: git diff of the unit over project-control/directives/**
acceptance_scenarios.expected: ZERO byte changes to any source-*.md, amendment, requirements.json, verification.json, or index.json; the ONLY directive-tree changes are the six digest-field values + one append-only audit_log entry per touched manifest (citing D-040:D-040-R003, ASCII-only note); locked_requirement_ids and every other manifest field byte-preserved.

acceptance_scenarios.input: adversarial fixtures: (a) a source with one CONTENT character changed (not line endings); (b) a requirements.json with one requirement body edited
acceptance_scenarios.expected: c2/c14 digest mismatch errors still raised - normalization forgives ONLY line-ending representation, never content; test proves the guard did not weaken.

acceptance_scenarios.input: the five CI control-plane commands run locally: test_project_control.py, validate_directive_compliance.py --check, test_directive_compliance.py, test_directive_reminder.py, test_readonly_agent_guard.py (+ test_agent_dispatch_guard.py)
acceptance_scenarios.expected: all EXIT 0 locally (stdlib-only, Windows/CRLF side) and the CI control-plane job green on the pushed head (ubuntu/LF side); no other CI job regresses.

risks: Normalization masking real tampering: AS-5 is the control - only CR bytes may be forgiven.

Manifest rewrite collateral: the manifests are CRLF-on-disk with specific indent; a JSON round-trip that reformats unrelated bytes breaks AS-4 byte-preservation and could flip OTHER digests - edit surgically, assert byte-identical round-trip outside the intended fields (the scratchpad/append_d038_m5t012.py pattern).
Hidden seventh digest: any digest site not normalized (or any additional stale value) resurfaces the red in CI - the pushed-head control-plane job is the only complete proof (AS-2/AS-6).

requirements_id_digest_sha256 is computed over a joined-string, not file bytes - do NOT touch it; migration_manifest digest currently passes both sides (LF on disk) - normalization must keep it passing.

Producer = orchestrator (control-plane precedent); reviewers G1 code-reviewer, G4 qa-engineer, G5 security-reviewer - no UI, no G3.
